title: ProductionRun, destructive Canvas, media, export, and cutover call surface

targetOwners.contracts: electron/shared/agentCapabilities owns canonical schemas and projection metadata
targetOwners.host: Project Agent Host owns only Thread/Turn/Item, human proposal lifecycle, TaskRef, and ArtifactRef
targetOwners.paidGeneration: ProductionRun owns run, gate, budget, provider job, receipt, recovery, cancellation, and artifact facts
targetOwners.standaloneExport: ExportJobManager plus ExportJobStore owns job lifecycle and the persisted audit manifest
targetOwners.canvasDelete: the existing Canvas proposal transaction and Undo journal own mutation and reversal
targetOwners.media: the existing active-project media index and local waveform decoder own source facts; capability results are safe projections
targetOwners.cutover: the existing archive-only manifest owns the one-way Agent switch; domain stores are preserved, not migrated

deletionDebt: handwritten Phase 4 aliases in canvasDescriptors.ts and timelineDescriptors.ts
Phase 4 TOOL_META and lock-policy literals in generationCanvas/agent/gate.ts
Phase 4 renderer direct-dispatch branches in applyCanvasToolCall.ts and timelineToolCall.ts
run_generation_batch mintSpendGrant -> runPlanWithToasts paid submission path
advertised and routable nomi_generate direct-provider MCP path plus its special progress/widget cases
any Host item or panel state that copies ProductionRun or ExportJob status instead of storing a reference

knownIntegrityGap.symptom: electron/export/exportJobs.ts can sanitize a current WebM transition manifest by replacing timeline.tracks with [] and assets with {} before persistence.
knownIntegrityGap.classRoot: the execution fallback manifest and the durable audit manifest are represented by one mutable shape, so compatibility can erase source truth.
knownIntegrityGap.requiredPrevention: persist an immutable canonical audit manifest and derive any backend-specific execution plan separately; add a root-cause contract and structural regression checks.

focusedTests: electron/export/exportJobs tests via focused integration files
hardFail: an Agent-paid action can reach mintSpendGrant, renderer generation queue, provider submit, or a second ledger without a ProductionRun and exact human receipt

the immutable provider-submission envelope digest differs between Host approval, the one correlated ProductionRun gate receipt, and the actual submitted provider payload, or a mismatch reaches budget reservation, ledger mutation, outbox intent, or provider submit
unknown provider submission is automatically retried or replayed after restart

any of get_media, inspect_media, search_media, inspect_source_range, or read_waveform accepts a stale/cross-project binding, exceeds its result/range/sample bound, exposes a local/relative/absolute/provider URL or bytes, or claims semantic understanding
a legacy nomi_generate direct path remains in catalog/list/schema, MCP protocol special cases, dispatcher/core routing, or generation-policy classification after the paid cutover
Host, TaskCenter, MCP, or UI copies business status and becomes a shadow task owner
a standalone export result exposes paths or records an audit manifest different from the actual canonical timeline/execution inputs

standalone export status/cancel trusts a renderer-supplied bare jobId without exact current immutable project identity, a ProductionRun-driven export creates a second ExportJob/ledger, or a TaskRef copies status/budget/provider/progress lifecycle facts

cutover writes its marker before every archive is durable, restores a legacy approval/Undo/execution/dual writer in a crash window, invalidates a domain task, resubmits submission_unknown work, or archives, clears, replays, or mutates ProductionRun, ExportJob, document, Canvas, media, or generated-result data

a capability loses its input/output reference role, uses an untyped cancel, fabricates an ETA, claims success without a project-bound reviewable artifact, or exposes a path/provider-bearing projection
a migrated alias remains independently described, gated, dispatched, or executed outside Registry and the canonical domain owner
